title: Counselor Desk Reference: Over-Estimate Share of Patient Payment Plans Add-On Charges
content:
When a charge is added to an active Patient Payment Plans plan as an add-on, a charge billed above the estimate given before the service is counted only in part.

**Rule.** Where the charge amount is above the estimate given before the service, only an over-estimate share of the part above the estimate is added: 0.50 on the High-Deductible Health Plan Account and the Self-Pay Account, 0.75 on any other financial class. Where the charge amount is not above its estimate, or the charge carries no estimate, the whole remaining balance is counted. The part left out stays on the financial account's standard statements.

**Counted amount.** The counted amount is the charge's remaining balance less the part above the estimate multiplied by one minus the over-estimate share. The part above the estimate is the charge amount less the estimate.

**Records read.** The financial class of the Patient Financial Account, the charge amount, the estimate carried on the charge, and the charge's remaining balance.

| Financial class of the Patient Financial Account | Charge amount compared with its estimate | Share of the part above the estimate that is added |
|---|---|---|
| High-Deductible Health Plan Account or Self-Pay Account | Above the estimate | 0.50 |
| Any other class | Above the estimate | 0.75 |
| Any class | Not above the estimate, or no estimate | Not applicable: the whole remaining balance is counted |

**Examples (hypothetical charge of 900.00, estimate 600.00, remaining balance 700.00).** The part above the estimate is 300.00.

- High-Deductible Health Plan Account: 0.50 of 300.00 is left out, so 150.00 is left out; the counted amount is 700.00 less 150.00, 550.00.
- Commercial HMO/EPO Account: 0.25 of 300.00 is left out, so 75.00 is left out; the counted amount is 625.00.
- A charge of 580.00 against the same estimate is not above it; the whole remaining balance is counted.
